knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the principal contractor buys a site that meets its own rules and a standard it can check. Your hourly rate, equipment list and business age are inputs, not what the contractor buys.
The lesson says a return-visit promise must be something you can deliver and afford, within a time you can staff. Unlimited, undefined or impossible promises are not sound.
The lesson says a measurable claim, such as a percentage of site inspections passed, must be backed by the record you can show. A famous endorsement, a discount or no evidence do not support a claim.

practicalCriteria: Applies the step to a real or simulated business decision and records the outcome
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Written output of the step (plan, offer, log or record)
stopWorkCriteria: Not applicable: business guidance; stop if an offer would make an unsubstantiated or misleading claim
